passage: In a small town in Bihar, Arjun's phone crawled on the home Wi-Fi the night before his online form was due. He opened the settings and began flipping things: the network band, power saving, a network reset, the DNS, airplane mode. Nothing seemed to help, so he kept going. At some point the phone stopped connecting at all. He couldn't remember what he had changed, or in which order, and next morning had to take it to his cousin Wasim, who fixed phones at the market. Wasim asked, 'What did you touch?' Arjun shrugged. The form deadline passed, and the phone needed a full reset.

qa.q: Who did Arjun take the phone to in the morning?
qa.a: Arjun took it to his cousin Wasim, who fixed phones at the market.

qa.q: How might Arjun have felt when Wasim asked 'What did you touch?'
qa.a: Arjun probably felt embarrassed and frustrated, since he could only shrug and had missed the deadline.

qa.q: What could Arjun have done differently that night?
qa.a: Arjun could have changed one setting at a time and written it down, undoing any change that did not help.

qa.q: How might Wasim see the situation?
qa.a: Wasim probably finds it hard to help, since there is no way to tell which change caused the fault, so a full reset is the only option.

passage:
The Wi-Fi in Santiago's Buenos Aires flat was fine on everyone's phone except his. Videos froze; messages took ages.
Saturday afternoon he decided to fix it himself. He switched the network band. Nothing. He turned on some battery saver setting. He changed the DNS, copied from a forum. He reset something called "network preferences". He turned off location. He switched the band back, he thought.
By evening his phone would not connect at all.
His friend Marek came over. "What did you change?"
Santiago opened his mouth, then closed it. "Lots of things. I don't remember which."
"So we can't undo it."
They ended up doing a full reset. Santiago lost his saved notes and every app setting.
He sat on the sofa, rubbing his face. "I made it worse, and I don't even know how."

qa.q: What did Santiago lose after the full reset?
qa.a: He lost his saved notes and every app setting.

qa.q: What was Santiago feeling as he sat on the sofa rubbing his face?
qa.a: He felt frustrated and embarrassed, because his random fixes had made things worse and he couldn't explain how.

qa.q: What approach would have suited Santiago better?
qa.a: Writing down each change and testing after it, one at a time, would have let him undo mistakes and see what actually helped.

qa.q: How might Marek see the afternoon?
qa.a: Marek is probably sympathetic but a little exasperated, since without a record of changes there was nothing to undo except a full reset.

grounding: It shows a teenager flipping phone settings at random without notes, forgetting what he changed and ending up worse off.

subtype: Approach: random changes with no record of what was tried [Pitfall]
passage:
In the boys' hostel of the residential school, Faizan's phone could barely load a page, while his roommates streamed videos. Study hour was his only free time, so he spent it poking at settings.
Airplane mode on and off. Private address off. Some "boost" option on. A proxy he found in a video comment. He tapped and toggled without writing anything down.
At the end of study hour, his phone showed "No internet" even in the corridor.
Elizabeth Ma'am, the house mistress, saw him scowling at the screen. "What have you changed?"
"Maybe eight things? Or ten?"
"And which of them made it worse?"
He shook his head.
She asked the school's tech assistant to reset it the next day. Faizan went a full day without his phone, and the only lesson he had was that he'd changed too much too fast.

qa.q: Who did Elizabeth Ma'am ask to reset the phone?
qa.a: She asked the school's tech assistant to reset it the next day.

qa.q: What was Faizan feeling when he could not say which change made it worse?
qa.a: He was frustrated and embarrassed, scowling at the screen after losing even the weak connection he had.

qa.q: What would you advise Faizan to do differently next time?
qa.a: Change one setting at a time, write it down and test, so he can undo anything that makes it worse.

qa.q: How does Elizabeth Ma'am see Faizan's struggle?
qa.a: She sees a boy who tried hard but without a method, which is why she asks what he changed and which change made it worse.

grounding: It shows a teenager changing phone settings at random without a record, ending up worse off and learning nothing reliable from the errors.
